heard: Galveston's weather chief raised hurricane flags the day before disaster. Earlier federal warnings had pointed toward Florida and the eastern Gulf. The Weather Service says Isaac Klein urged residents to move to higher ground. On September 8, a 15-foot surge swallowed Galveston. The island's highest ground was just 8.7 feet above sea level. More than 8,000 died, including Klein's pregnant wife. It remains America's deadliest natural disaster.
